rules.when: Research needing current external facts: news, releases, product state or up-to-date documentation.
rules.why: Quick lookups need live search, not frontier reasoning: Flash, Sol, Grok and Antigravity Sonnet each cover a separate pool, so quota decides among them.

rules.when: Generate images or visual assets: icons, illustrations, logos or mockup art.
rules.why: Pi exposes image generation; Flash keeps asset calls fast without requiring frontier reasoning.

rules.when: Review or audit another worker's diff, PR or design. Not for implementing fixes.
rules.why: Opus is the strongest reviewer; Sol xhigh reviews from a separate pool and family. Quota ranking does not enforce family separation, so choose Sol explicitly for Claude-written work.

rules.when: Recon, narrow file lookup or trivial mechanical edits: renames, formatting or typos. Not current-facts research or whole-codebase mapping.
rules.why: Low-effort work needs no frontier reasoning: Haiku, Flash, Terra and Grok each cover one pool, and Terra low beats Luna on quality and speed.

rules.when: Ordinary implementation, bounded bug fixes or focused tests with a clear path. Not risky multi-file refactors or unresolved root causes.
rules.why: Sonnet handles routine coding; Sol medium and Grok cover separate pools. One candidate per quota scope, because candidates sharing a scope tie in quota ranking.

rules.when: Large multi-file implementation or risky refactoring with a known goal. Not unresolved root causes, architecture decisions or previously failed approaches.
rules.why: Fable high is the fastest Claude and Sol xhigh near-frontier, each from its own pool, so quota decides; Grok xhigh is weaker spare capacity.

rules.when: Hardest work: unresolved root causes, architecture decisions, ambiguous design or work that already failed with an everyday implementation approach.
rules.why: Opus scores highest on reasoning; Sol xhigh is the frontier candidate from a separate pool, so quota decides between them.

rules.when: Read-only mapping of an entire codebase: feature maps, capability inventories or architecture surveys. Produce a report; change no files.
rules.why: Sonnet and Sol read across many files; both Claude routes expose their respective pools when available.

rules.when: Evaluation judging: score finished outputs or transcripts against a fixed rubric. Not code review or implementation.
rules.why: Haiku is a small judge from a different family than Codex-written work; Luna medium is the separate-pool alternative.
